definitions.explanation: Meat that has been finely chopped or ground using a grinder. Used as an ingredient in dishes such as hamburgers, meatballs, and gyoza.

examples.japanese: {挽肉|ひきにく}を{買|か}ってきて。
{豚|ぶた}{挽肉|ひきにく}で{餃子|ぎょうざ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made gyoza with ground pork.

examples.japanese: ハンバーグには{牛|ぎゅう}と{豚|ぶた}の{合|あ}い{挽|び}き{肉|にく}を{使|つか}うとおいしい。
examples.english: Using a blend of ground beef and pork makes the best hamburger steak.

notes:
Also commonly written in hiragana as ひき{肉|にく} or in katakana as ひき{肉|にく}. The kanji {挽|ひ}く means to grind.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牛|ぎゅう}{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground beef)
- {豚|ぶた}{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground pork)
- {鶏|とり}{挽肉|ひきにく} (ground chicken)
- {合|あ}い{挽|び}き{肉|にく} (mixed ground meat, usually beef and pork)

SUPERMARKET LABELS:
At Japanese supermarkets, ground meat is typically labeled by animal: {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}, {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}, {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}, or {合|あ}いびき{肉|にく}.
